title: Premarket · Monday 9/21

headline.title: Crypto took the weekend and did not give it back. Bitcoin printed $85,229.44, a level not seen since January 29, and the equity proxies are moving with it: MSTR +7.19%, HOOD +5.32%, COIN +5.18% — on top of Friday's +16.39%, +9.12% and +11.66%. Futures are firmly bid: S&P +0.7% above fair value, Nasdaq 100 +1.1%, Dow +0.9%.
headline.summary: The bid is being paid for by oil and bonds, and the oil half does not add up on the headlines alone. WTI −2.7% to $97.59, through $100 to the downside — on a weekend when the Houthis attacked Riyadh. Crude falling into a strike on the Saudi capital only makes sense next to the other number: Saudi Arabia moved nearly 3.0M barrels a day through the Strait of Hormuz over the last six days, and Trump is signalling he will meet Iran's president at this week's UN General Assembly. The market is pricing the diplomacy, not the missiles. Yields came with it — 2-year −3bp to 4.71%, 10-year −5bp to 4.95%. There is no US economic data at all today, which leaves the tape to positioning ahead of Trump–Xi on 9/24.

overview:
Friday settled three things this book called. MU cleared 986.20 and closed 1,015.80, +3.92% — through $1,000 for the first time, on the way to 9/30 earnings. GOOGL pinned: it gapped to 357.31, faded all day, and closed 349.54 against the 349.50 level named here that morning — four cents. Triple-witching pinning, which is why the note said wait for the 30-minute close rather than buy the gap. MCD never broke — 250.45 high, 247.65 low, closed 248.24 back inside. No trade, correctly.

And one it got wrong. This book read STX's $848M mid-side print against a downtrend and wrote that “price says the sellers are still in control.” STX closed Friday +6.93% and is +3.26% again this morning at 886.80. Mid is interest, not direction — and then a direction got read into it anyway. The print was the tell.

Crypto is the trend. Regulators cleared a path for tokenized stocks last week; COIN has now run +11.66% then +5.18% premarket.

ACN cuts both ways. Down 4.73% Friday on the Guggenheim cut, then +4.34% this morning on an Anthropic partnership — at least $1B each over five years on embedded AI safety evaluators.

Also moving: WBD +7.23% and PSKY +6.17% on settlement talks over the $81B deal. CIEN +6.04%, Evercore to Outperform, $550. NVO −4.30% — 2030 targets underwhelmed and GLP-1 vision-loss suits landed. HPQ −4.59% on 2027 PC declines and withheld guidance.

+7.23% with PSKY +6.17%, on reports Paramount Skydance is discussing a $1.5B investment in California production as a concession to resolve legal challenges to the $81B deal.
Gapping clear of both Friday's 28.13 high and Thursday's 28.45. That is the level — 28.45 is the line that matters, and it is well below spot. Merger-arb gaps do not retrace like momentum gaps.

The concessions reported: retain both California studio lots, penalties if Paramount fails to produce 30 films annually, potential cable-channel sales, and a board to preserve CNN's editorial independence.
California and 11 other states sued to block it on antitrust grounds. The settlement talks are the hurdle, so this is binary headline risk in both directions.
Not a Strat setup. It is a legal process priced in headlines — on the board so it is not a surprise, not because it is tradeable on a level.

darkpool.note: No fresh single-name tape for this session yet — what follows is Thursday night's board, and Friday's action has already spoken to the most important line in it. The largest ex-ETF print was STX $848M at the mid, after hours, and this book read it against the downtrend as sellers in control. STX then closed +6.93% Friday and is +3.26% again this morning. The print was the tell; the interpretation was not. Storage-and-memory held the crown with TSM $624M (ask) behind it, and cumulative flow remains the memory trade in miniature: MU $3.1B (bid) on top into its 9/30 earnings, then NVDA $3.0B (ask) and AVGO $2.1B (bid) — the two biggest cumulative names on opposite sides. MU has since cleared $1,000 and that $1000C sweep dated 10/02 is in the money. On the ETF side the trackers led for a ninth straight session with SPY $1.1B (ask), VOO $973M and IVV $972M, all three at the ask into the bounce after printing at the bid into the decision. A side is a lean, not a verdict — and the STX line above is what it costs to forget the second half of that sentence.
darkpool.right_note: Carried from Friday morning and now resolved: GOOGL's $50M bid print preceded a session that gapped to 357.31 and closed 349.54 — four cents above the level named here, pinned into the expiration. The largest block on either board was AMGN $460P 10/16/26 at $131.4M, still open, October expiry. Size is the signal, direction is not.
